docs.title: Gabe's Cafe
docs.text: Welcome to my site! Here I will post some personal notes, blogs, and resources from my journey learning Japanese, various bits of media that I have consumed, tech related things or anything else I think is cool.

docs.title: 30 Days In
docs.text: So far, I have kept my studies up consistently for the past 30 days. I am writing this on 9/15/2024, and my first day of Anki was on 8/13/2024. For the last 30 days, I mainly followed the steps outlined by The Moe Way, with some additional feedback from sites like Tatsumoto Ren's, but the basic tenant of everything that I did during the last 30 days revolved around consistently doing Anki for vocab, gramamr studies, and immersion.

docs.title: Anki
docs.text:
The core vocabulary deck that I used is the Kaishi 1.5k deck. Starting out Anki was pretty rough, but I have been consistent with it. I feel like my retention is still fairly poor, so this is something that I am looing to work on, though it has been slowly climbing as I gain the ability to recognize kanji.

I also utilized the RRTK450 deck. This is suppossed to teach radicals and mnemonics to remember kanji. I have not really seemed to have much success with this deck. I think going forward the plan is to drop it for something else.

docs.title: Grammar
docs.text: In the beginning, I was utilizing Tae Kim's Grammar Guide, as typically I prefer to read over watching videos. The Moe Way community typically recommends Cure Dolly, but after doing my own research I decided to ignore that advice. Probably 10 days or so into studying, I started to find Tae Kim incredibly hard to sit through. The content is good, but very academic a lot of the time. I switched to what a lot of people recommend, which is Cure Dolly Youtube videos. These explanations felt a lot more natural, and concepts began to stick better. I am about 2/3 of the way through the playlist containing all of her videos..

docs.title: Immersion
docs.text: I started out not doing as much immersion as I probably should have, but have tried to rectify that recently. I chose K-ON as an anime that I could immerse with, and started out using the "Subtitle Tutor" method, wherein I watched it English subbed, then raw. I have now switched to JP subs to try to get more reading practice. Once I finish an episode I grab the condensed audio for some passive immersion where I can. Nihongo con Teppei has also been a great source of passive listening for me, and I throw it on in the background whenever I am working and look up words when I can. For reading practice, I have been using the よつばと! manga. Right now I am still struggling a lot, and am about halfway through the first volume, but can tell things are getting quite a lot better.

docs.title: Go Forward Plan
docs.text: Going forward, I plan to ditch the RRTK450 deck and try WaniKani. I have heard some people say that dedicated kanji study is unnecessary, while others very much disagree. Currently, I feel like I am wasting my time with the RRTK450 deck though, so hopefully WaniKani is better. Currently have made an account and am on the free trial. For grammar, I have around 20 Cure Dolly videos to go, and then will probably go back through Tae Kim to see if I can fill in any gaps. There is a Dictionary of Japanese Grammar Anki deck that I may check out as well. Once I get to about 1,000 words, I plan to take the plunge on immersion and start a Visual Novel. I have H2O: Footprints in the Sand, bookmarked as one to try as my first. Currently I am ~700 words in, so this will be in the next couple of weeks. Once I do this, I also plan to start a mining deck. I also want to try diversifying and increasing my immmersion. I have already begun watching some Japanese language Youtube channels meant for immersion learners, and will probably expand my podcast listening.

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text: This has been a super great experience. These methods have largely allowed me to learn the language while also consuming content that I actually enjoy doing. I have settled into a rythm now of Anki, grammar, and immersion pretty much every day, and it is just what I do now.
